image_prompt: Extreme macro photograph of a freshly applied paint surface in deep navy blue. The paint is wet — a soft wet sheen visible across the entire surface. A roller mark texture is visible, showing the application. Strong raking light from the left revealing the surface topography. The boundary between a wet painted section and an unpainted section runs diagonally through the frame. 100mm macro, f/8. Deep rich grading, navy saturated. 4:5 portrait. No text, no logos.

text_overlay.subtext:
Do not hang anything before that.
Do not wipe it before that.

caption:
This is the most misunderstood timeline in home painting.

Dry means touch-dry — you can apply the next coat. Cure means fully hardened — the surface can take impact, friction, and cleaning without damage.

Most people hang frames, place furniture against walls, and start wiping surfaces within days of painting. The result: marks, scuffs, and peeling that look like a bad paint job. It was not the paint. It was the timing.

Save this. Share it with whoever just got their home painted.
